matches.note: R1 identifies the same flaw: the Jasypt password is derived from constant row fields busId/version, so anyone with DB read access can decrypt the key and forge JWTs.

unmatched_reported.note: fetchSecret never decrypts, so a row that cannot be decrypted passes the bootstrap check and the app boots, which contradicts the documented fail-at-startup behaviour.
findOneByVersionAndBusId ignores EntityStatus, so marking the row INACTIVE does not stop the key from being used to sign tokens.
The reviewer says the method has no callers, so the stale cache is latent and has no current trigger.
Map.of throws NPE on null values, so null arguments raise an NPE instead of the intended SecException, and callers that catch SecException do not handle it.
The reviewer says getKey has no callers, so the risk depends entirely on future code.
The performance cost is speculative and unquantified; the reviewer itself asks for profiling.
